name: Dataflow Gen2, pipelines, mirroring and medallion design

why.matters: In Fabric, data preparation moves out of each semantic model into shared, scheduled layers. That's what makes one definition possible for many models.
why.failure: Five models each clean the same export with slightly different Power Query steps, and five "Revenue" numbers appear (Sprint 05, again).
why.use: Bronze (raw, as landed), silver (cleaned, conformed), gold (star schema for models); Dataflow Gen2 for Power Query-style transformations, pipelines to orchestrate, mirroring to replicate operational databases continuously.
why.avoid: Medallion layers for their own sake on small data. Two layers are fine if they're clearly owned.

verified.context: Dataflow Gen2, pipelines, mirroring (SQL Server, updated 2026-07-06) and medallion docs (Microsoft Learn)

asg.t: Move the clean-up out of the model
asg.brief: Turn the Beginner RawOrdersExport clean-up into a Dataflow Gen2 that writes a silver table, so every model reads the same cleaned data.
req: Same rules as Beginner (header and total rows, dates, prices, duplicates).
Output destination: a lakehouse or warehouse table, with an explicit schema.
Refresh on a schedule; show two models reading the same table.
asg.exp: A silver table with 27 rows and 8 columns, refreshed by the dataflow; both models read it, so a fix in the dataflow fixes both.

asg.t: Design the medallion layers for Northwind
asg.brief: Following ADR-009 (Sprint 09), design bronze, silver and gold for the sales data: what lands where, which tool writes each layer, who owns it, and which data-quality checks run between layers.
req: Mirroring or pipelines for the operational database.
Where deduplication, currency conversion and the test-customer rule live.
The gold tables the semantic model reads.
asg.exp: Bronze: mirrored NorthwindDW and landed files (owner: data engineering). Silver: deduplicated, typed, conformed tables with DQ tests (dedup, test customer, FX). Gold: star schema materialised in a Warehouse (FactSales, FactReturns, dimensions), read by a Direct Lake on OneLake model. Tests block promotion from silver to gold.

asg.brief: Build (or design) a pipeline that runs the nightly sequence so the semantic model only shows data that passed its tests.
req: Steps: refresh the dataflow or wait for mirroring, run data-quality checks, load gold, refresh (frame) the semantic model, run model tests, notify.
What happens when a step fails.
asg.exp: A pipeline: Dataflow → stored procedure DQ checks (fail stops the run) → gold load → semantic model refresh activity → test query → notify team channel; failures stop downstream steps and alert, so users keep seeing the last good data.

int.q: Dataflow Gen2 vs Power Query in the model?
int.a: Both use Power Query. Dataflow Gen2 runs once and writes to a destination (lakehouse, warehouse and others) that many models and tools can read; Power Query in the model only serves that model. Use dataflows for shared preparation.

Continuously replicates a supported database (for example SQL Server 2016 and later, through a gateway for on-premises) into OneLake as Delta tables with a SQL analytics endpoint, without building ETL. Replication compute is free; querying uses capacity.

Bronze holds raw data as landed, silver holds cleaned and conformed data, gold holds business-ready models (often star schemas). Each layer has an owner and tests between layers, so problems are caught before reports.

int.q: Why orchestrate refresh in a pipeline rather than schedule each item?
int.a: Dependencies: the model should refresh only after its data is loaded and tested. A pipeline encodes the order, stops on failure and notifies, so users never see half-loaded data.

ass.q: Five models clean the same export differently. Best fix in Fabric:
o: Copy the best query into all five
One Dataflow Gen2 writing a shared table that all five read
ass.why: One shared preparation step, one definition.

ass.q: Mirroring an on-premises SQL Server into Fabric requires:
o: A supported SQL Server version and a data gateway (on-premises or VNet) for connectivity
ass.why: On-premises sources are reached through a gateway; SQL Server 2016–2022 uses CDC, 2025 uses the change feed with Azure Arc.

ass.q: Draw the Northwind data flow from source to report on one page, marking owners and test points.
ass.hint: NorthwindDW → mirror (bronze) → silver tables → gold warehouse → Direct Lake model → reports; tests at silver→gold and after model refresh.
